newsitem.title: USA: Southwest Air Q1 results tough to match - CFO.
newsitem.headline: Southwest Air Q1 results tough to match - CFO.

text.p: Southwest Airlines Co is showing strong second-quarter revenue trends but will be hard-pressed to match its impressive earnings performance from the first quarter, Chief Financial Officer Gary Kelly said.

"It is safe to say that, while first quarter earnings were up 54 percent, I think it is going to be real tough to come anywhere close to matching that in the second quarter," Kelly told reporters on a conference call.

Kelly said Southwest's second quarter results would also face a difficult match-up to the same period last year, when Southwest reported record quarterly earnings, because the carrier is now paying a 10 percent excise tax that was not being applied a year ago. "It is going to make revenues growth comparison much more difficult," he said.

But Kelly stressed revenue trends were firm and pointed out that fuel prices had dipped from around $0.70 per gallon in the first quarter to $0.61-$0.62 per gallon now. "We will still realize some strong revenues performance, I just don't know how it will compare to last year."
Southwest earlier reported first quarter earnings of $50.8 million, or $0.34 per share, way above the Wall Street consensus estimate of $0.23 per share. Total operating revenues were $887.1 million.

Kelly said first quarter profits were boosted by moderate fare increases in selected markets, higher demand from business travellers and strong performances from Southwest's services into Florida and Providence, Rhode Island.
"It (the East coast) is a rapidly maturing market for us and is performing very, very well," Kelly said.
Kelly said Southwest "may have pushed fares too hard" on a very small number of routes but the market shows no sign of flagging.
"As a general rule, the demand for air travel is very strong and we don't see any signs of weakening in that demand," he said.
